full_caption: Applegate Commons Homeowners Association, Inc., Appellant, v. Lucian Ellsworth-Vane, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Applegate Commons Homeowners Association, Inc., the association governing the Blackthorn Ridge subdivision, brought this action to enjoin Lucian Ellsworth-Vane from maintaining a detached structure at 77 Pennyroyal Court, Rooksbury, NR in violation of Article V of the recorded declaration.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Covenants are construed in favor of the free use of land. Ambiguity in a restriction is resolved against the party seeking to enforce it, and a restriction will not be extended by implication to conduct not fairly within its terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Article V prohibits 'any outbuilding, shed or accessory structure exceeding one hundred twenty square feet.' The structure erected by Lucian Ellsworth-Vane measures 140 square feet and is therefore within the plain reach of the restriction.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The association's architectural review committee denied the application by letter dated October 23, 2004. The declaration requires that denials state the specific ground relied upon; the letter recited only that the proposal was 'not in harmony with the community.'

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The defense of changed conditions requires a showing that the character of the neighborhood has so altered that the original purpose of the restriction can no longer be achieved. Isolated violations elsewhere in the subdivision do not meet that standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Fines totaling $100 were imposed without the hearing required by the bylaws. A fine imposed in disregard of the association's own procedural requirements is void, without regard to the merits of the underlying violation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: The association waived enforcement as to fence height by failing to act against 19 comparable violations over a period of 10 years. Selective enforcement of a covenant against one owner, after acquiescence in like violations by others, is inequitable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Restrictive covenants are enforceable servitudes running with the land where they are (1) in writing, (2) intended to run, (3) touching and concerning the land, and (4) recorded so as to give notice to successors.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Assessments levied under Article XII became a lien on the lot upon recording of the notice of assessment. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage recorded earlier in time but superior to subsequent encumbrances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The business judgment rule shields the board's maintenance and budgeting decisions from judicial second-guessing where the board acted within its authority, on an informed basis, and in the honest belief that the action served the association.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: A discretionary architectural approval power must be exercised reasonably and in good faith. A denial that states no articulable standard is arbitrary and will not support injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: We reverse the injunction as to the fence and affirm as to the accessory structure. The award of fines is vacated in its entirety.

sections.heading: RIDER 3 — ENFORCEMENT, FINES AND HEARING RIGHTS
sections.text: Before imposing any fine, the Board shall give the owner written notice of the alleged violation and an opportunity to be heard before the Board or a committee of at least three members who are not officers. Fines shall not exceed $100 per violation nor $5,000 in the aggregate for a continuing violation. A fine imposed without the notice and hearing required by this Rider is void.

sections.heading: RIDER 4 — LEASING RESTRICTION
sections.text: No Lot may be leased for a term of less than 9 months, and no more than 4 percent of the Lots may be leased at any one time. An owner in possession on the date this Rider was recorded is exempt as to that Lot until title is transferred. This Rider does not apply to a lease to a family member of the owner or to occupancy incident to a mortgagee's possession following foreclosure.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Notice
sections.text: Every notice required or permitted shall be in writing and shall be deemed given: on personal delivery; on the third business day after deposit in the United States mail, certified, return receipt requested, postage prepaid; or on the next business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier. Notices to a party shall be sent to the address last furnished by that party in writing. Electronic mail alone does not constitute notice unless the recipient acknowledges receipt in writing.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 15 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.
